'''John Philip Burrows''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}} (born 16 August 1954)<ref name=whoswho/> is professor of the [[Atmospheric physics|Physics of the Ocean and Atmosphere]] and Director of the Institutes of Environmental Physics and [[Remote Sensing]] at the [[University of Bremen]].<ref name=bremen/> He is also a Fellow of the UK [[Centre for Ecology and Hydrology|Centre for Ecology and Hydrology (CEH)]], part of the [[Natural Environment Research Council|Natural Environment Research Council (NERC)]].<ref name=frs/>

==Education==
Burrows was educated at West Park Grammar School in [[St Helens, Merseyside]].<ref name=cv>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130428060821/http://cacgp.chemistry.uoc.gr/cvs_cacgp_07/professor_john_p_CV_new.htm|archive-date=2013-04-28|url=http://cacgp.chemistry.uoc.gr/cvs_cacgp_07/professor_john_p_CV_new.htm|title=Prof. John P. Burrows ICACGP president|publisher=ouc.gr|location=Crete}}</ref> He went on to study at [[Trinity College, Cambridge]], where he was awarded a Bachelor of Arts degree in [[Natural Sciences (Cambridge)|Natural Sciences]] in 1975 followed by a PhD in 1978 for research investigating [[free radical]] reactions by laser [[magnetic resonance imaging|magnetic resonance]] supervised by [[Brian Arthur Thrush]].<ref name=cv/><ref>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=University of Cambridge|title=Study of Free Radical Reactions by Laser Magnetic Resonance|first= John Philip|last=Burrows|year=1978|url=http://ethos.bl.uk/OrderDetails.do?uin=uk.bl.ethos.450310|oclc=500395836}}</ref><ref name=googlescholar>{{Google Scholar id|John Philip Burrows}}</ref>

==Career==
Following his PhD, Burrows was a [[postdoctoral researcher]] at the [[Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics|Center for Astrophysics {{!}} Harvard & Smithsonian]] in [[Cambridge, Massachusetts]]. From 1979 to 1982 he worked at the [[Atomic Energy Research Establishment|Atomic Energy Research Establishment (AERE)]] in [[Harwell, Oxfordshire|Harwell]] followed by ten years at the [[Max Planck Institute for Chemistry]] in [[Mainz]]. He was appointed a professor at the University of Bremen in 1992 where he has worked since.<ref name=bremen>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130420175352/http://www.pep.uni-bremen.de/about_pep/staff/john_burrows.htm|archive-date=2013-04-20|url=http://www.pep.uni-bremen.de/about_pep/staff/john_burrows.htm|title=Prof. Dr. John P. Burrows: Physics and Chemistry of the Atmosphere|publisher=uni-bremen.de|location=Bremen}}</ref>

==Research==
Burrows' research<ref name=googlescholar/> has contributed to our scientific understanding of air pollution, the [[ozone layer]], the [[Near space|upper atmosphere]],<ref name=RichterBurrows2005>{{cite journal|last1=Richter|first1=Andreas|last2=Burrows|first2=John P.|last3=Nüß|first3=Hendrik|last4=Granier|first4=Claire|last5=Niemeier|first5=Ulrike|title=Increase in tropospheric nitrogen dioxide over China observed from space|journal=Nature|volume=437|issue=7055|year=2005|pages=129–132|doi=10.1038/nature04092|pmid=16136141|bibcode=2005Natur.437..129R |s2cid=4360979}}</ref> [[biogeochemistry]] and [[climate change]]. He and his co-workers have studied the kinetics and [[spectroscopy]] of key atmospheric free radicals and gases, developed innovative ''[[in situ]]'' trace atmospheric measurement techniques, and pioneered the passive [[remote sensing]] of atmospheric constituents and surface parameters. Working closely with the [[German Aerospace Center|German Aerospace Center (DLR)]], the [[European Space Agency|European Space Agency (ESA)]] and [[NASA]], he initiated and led scientifically the [[SCIAMACHY]] project,<ref name=scimachy>{{cite journal|last1=Bovensmann|first1=H.|last2=Burrows|first2=J. P.|last3=Buchwitz|first3=M.|last4=Frerick|first4=J.|last5=Noël|first5=S.|last6=Rozanov|first6=V. V.|last7=Chance|first7=K. V.|last8=Goede|first8=A. P. H.|title=SCIAMACHY: Mission Objectives and Measurement Modes|journal=Journal of the Atmospheric Sciences|volume=56|issue=2|year=1999|pages=127–150|doi=10.1175/1520-0469(1999)056<0127:SMOAMM>2.0.CO;2|bibcode=1999JAtS...56..127B }}</ref> which resulted in the satellite based measurements of the instruments Global Ozone Monitoring Experiment (GOME)<ref name=GOME>{{cite journal|last1=Burrows|first1=John P.|last2=Weber|first2=Mark|last3=Buchwitz|first3=Michael|last4=Rozanov|first4=Vladimir|last5=Ladstätter-Weißenmayer|first5=Annette|last6=Richter|first6=Andreas|last7=DeBeek|first7=Rüdiger|last8=Hoogen|first8=Ricarda|last9=Bramstedt|first9=Klaus|last10=Eichmann|first10=Kai-Uwe|last11=Eisinger|first11=Michael|last12=Perner|first12=Dieter|title=The Global Ozone Monitoring Experiment (GOME): Mission Concept and First Scientific Results|journal=Journal of the Atmospheric Sciences|volume=56|issue=2|year=1999|pages=151–175|doi=10.1175/1520-0469(1999)056<0151:TGOMEG>2.0.CO;2|bibcode=1999JAtS...56..151B |s2cid=67774583 }}</ref> on ESA [[European Remote-Sensing Satellite|ERS-2]] (1995–2011), SCIAMACHY on ESA [[Envisat]] (2002 -2012), GOME-2 on [[EUMETSAT]] [[Metop]] Series (2006–2022), and the concepts GeoSCIA/GeoTROPE, now developed as European Union [[Copernicus Programme]] Sentinel 4, and CarbonSat/CarbonSat Constellation.<ref name=frs/>

==Awards and honours==
Burrows is a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science|American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)]], [[American Geophysical Union|American Geophysical Union (AGU)]], the [[International Union of Geodesy and Geophysics|International Union of Geodesy and Geophysics (IUGG)]], the [[Centre for Ecology and Hydrology]] and member of IAA. His research accolades include being awarded the following: the [[Committee on Space Research|Committee on Space Research (COSPAR)]] William Nordberg Medal in 2006, the [[NASA Group Achievement Award]] in 2008, the ''[[Journal of Quantitative Spectroscopy and Radiative Transfer]]'' (JQSRT) Milestone Paper Award in 2010, Haagen-Smit Prize 2012, EGU Vilhelm Bjerknes Medal 2013, IUGG Silver Medal IUGG 2015, and the [[Alfred Wegener]] Medal EGU 2016.<ref name=frs/> Burrows was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 2016|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 2016]].<ref name=frs>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/john-burrows-12848/ |title=Professor John Burrows FRS |publisher=[[Royal Society]] |archive-date=2016-04-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160429122608/https://royalsociety.org/people/john-burrows-12848/ |location=London |author=Anon |year=2016 }} One or more of the preceding sentences incorporates text from the royalsociety.org website where: {{blockquote|"All text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]]." --{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies |access-date=2016-03-09 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150925220834/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |archive-date=2015-09-25 }}}}</ref>
